elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Revised 2.2 reads: "Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services, and Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation." The prior "sole and exclusive provider ... throughout the term" language is removed, and 2.1 (no minimum or purchase commitment) and 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges no exclusivity commitment) are consistent with, not contradicted by, the new text.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity obligation is imposed on Customer at all after the edit, so there is no exclusivity requiring category limitation. The preferred outcome subsumes the fallback constraint.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity period exists in the revised 2.2, so no duration cap is needed.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no exclusivity to terminate; the appointment is expressly non-exclusive.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity obligation remains that would require a delivery-date exit trigger.

reasons: The single edit is confined to Section 2.2, converting "sole and exclusive provider ... throughout the term" into a non-exclusive appointment plus an express confirmation that Customer bears no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation — exactly the preferred element and nothing more.
Sections 2.1 and 12.3 are retained verbatim; no favourable Customer language was deleted and no extras (survival tails, procedures, remedies, damages categories) were added.

No exclusivity running in Customer's favour existed in the cited text, so none was stripped; the retained 12.3 acknowledgement now aligns with rather than contradicts 2.2, curing the prior internal conflict.

No undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced; "hosted analytics services" is retained from the original clause and commercial mechanics (Order Form ordering, no minimum commitment) survive unchanged.

Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies, no requirements/sole-supplier obligation remains on Customer, and the minimality and element-coverage gates pass — consistent with substantive reading of the rendered language.
